text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.9% today, extending a sharp 9% decline over two weeks as the refining sector unwinds from what had been a highly profitable period. The underlying reason is plainly stated in recent headlines: the "epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding." Refineries have been running hot at 95.7% capacity and profiting from high crude prices and tight supply, but that trade is now reversing as market conditions normalize and investors rotate out of energy.

The geopolitical backdrop that helped fuel refiner gains—tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi strikes on Saudi refineries, and U.S. sanctions on Iran—initially supported oil prices and refinery margins. With crude near $90 per barrel and storage levels elevated, however, the acute supply concerns that drove the refinery boom appear to be fading, and the market is reassessing whether that outsized profitability can persist.
